title: observability digest scratchpad — midday dump
content:
MIDDAY TRIGGERS & QUICK DUMP (notes to self)

2026-03-12 11:08 PST — rationale: quick triage for AcmePay report
- Customer: AcmePay (on Dedicated). Report: streaming responses occasionally stop mid-stream (user-visible) ~ 11:00–11:20 PST.
- Symptom: server sends final chunk then silence OR connection resets on client side. Shows as status=partial_stream in our request logs.
- Seen on model variant: gpt-4o-stream-quant-v2 primarily (canary pool).

Immediate quick checks (what I ran)
- Grafana panels: token-latency-95, stream-drop-rate, conn-reset-count (dashboard id 312).
- Quick query (prod logs):
  SELECT count(*) FROM request_logs WHERE model = 'gpt-4o-stream-quant-v2' AND outcome = 'partial_stream' AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour';
  -> result: 47 partial streams in last 45m, baseline ~3/h
- Canaries: canary pool CPU spiked at 10:58 -> prefetch queue grew -> memory reclaim started GC-like pauses on a subset of instances.
- Noted: autoscaler bumped burst pool at 11:02 but routing policy still sent some traffic to old canary instances.

Hypotheses (ordered by plausibility)
1) kv-cache eviction thrash on quantized models when sequence length > 2048 -> longer KV writes cause kernel stall -> streaming thread misses keep-alive -> client sees partial stream. (See debug trace attached in INF-5678)
2) Networking: ephemeral connection reset between LB and GPU host due to transient NIC error (less likely; would show server-level conn resets).
3) Runtime bug in new tokenizer boundary handling in v2 build (only on canary hosts).

Short term mitigation options (notes for on-call / SRE)
- Roll traffic away from canary pool (policy: route to stable variant gpt-4o-stream-quant-v1) until canary nodes are reproved. Action: Liam to flip route rule for AcmePay.
- Increase kv-cache size on affected hosts (if safe) and monitor miss rate. Quick command: /infra/ssh -> sudo sysctl -w runtime.kv_cache.max_entries=200000 (confirm change impact).
- If partial_stream persists > 30m, consider immediate rollback of canary image (PR #1423).

Follow-ups to document / tickets to update
- INF-5678: add full stacktrace from 11:02 on canary-11 host (grab from /var/log/runtime/streams.log).
- Create a short postmortem draft if customer impact > 30m or > 100 requests affected. Use template: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/PM-template
- Add checklist item to release notes for quant builds: monitor kv-cache eviction rate and token-latency-95 for 1h after rollout.

Todays quick todo (me)
- [ ] Pull host-level dmesg for canary-11 and canary-12 -> saved at /tmp/priya-dmesg-2026-03-12.txt
- [x] Query logs for partial_stream counts (ran at 11:10)
- [ ] Slack customer-success with update for AcmePay (notify: "routing to stable variant, investigating")
- [ ] Add notes to INF-5678 with my raw observations and attach the SQL output + grafana snapshots
- [ ] Coordinate with Liam to flip routing if we see repeat spikes after 15m

Observability anomalies I want to follow beyond AcmePay
- KV-cache miss spike at 03:12 UTC on 2026-03-12 (seen across 3 regions) — correlate with nightly model cache compaction job? Tagging: storage-team.
- Dashboard "per-route cost" shows unexpected token-cost increase for /v1/generate when model = 'redwood-mini-embed' 2026-03-11 22:00–23:30 (maybe billing metadata issue).
- Alert noise: pager for "node-disk-low" frying on ephemeral infra hosts; need to mark noisy hosts in alert suppression for 24h while infra reclaims.

Quick runbook snippets (copyable)
- Roll routing to stable variant (cli):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-internal/route/update -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"customer":"AcmePay","route":"stable-gpt4o"}'
- Get partial stream examples (logs):
  rg "partial_stream" /var/log/runtime/streams.log | head -n 50 > /tmp/partial_examples.txt
- Temporarily disable canary: ./infra/cmds/disable-canary --pool canary-quant-v2 --reason "partial stream"

Questions / notes to myself for root cause
- Did the kernel version differ on the canary hosts? (compare /proc/version across hosts).
- Is there any memory-pressure metric correlation with tokenization latency (per-host tokenization_ms)?
- Confirm whether client-side backoff pattern changed for AcmePay SDK (ask CS: Maya).

Random brainstorm (less formal)
- Could streaming client hit edge timeout at ~60s while server is still trying to stream last tokens because of a downstream disk sync? Add heartbeat chunk every 10 tokens to reduce client timeouts? (Pros/cons: extra tokens increase cost and might mask underlying problem)

Messages to send (short drafts)
- To AcmePay CS thread: "Quick update: we routed your traffic away from the canary pool and are seeing partial_stream events drop to baseline. We're continuing to investigate kv-cache eviction behavior. ETA 2–3 hours for full update."
- To #infra-alerts: "Temporarily suppress node-disk-low for ephemeral hosts h1-{01..06} for 2h while we drain and repair."

Other micro-notes
- Attach snapshots: grafana_snapshot_token-latency-95_2026-03-12.png, stream-drop-rate_11-10.png. (Saved to /home/priya/snapshots/)
- PR 1423: includes tokenizer boundary fix — check unit tests coverage around boundary-case #7.

End of midday dump. Will revisit at ~14:00 PST after we see routing changes.

-- priya

(rough, messy — meant as working notes for handoff; move to INF-5678 if confirmed)
